planting.note: Direct sow in warm soil; semi-dwarf, few-branched habit allows closer in-row spacing than tall heirloom cowhorn types.

directions: Cajun King is a Louisiana market-garden okra prized for its straight, dark-green, ribbed pods that stay tender well past typical harvest size, reportedly up to 15 inches, without becoming tough or fibrous. The semi-dwarf plants branch less than many heirloom types, maturing roughly 10 days earlier than Clemson Spineless and producing heavily over a long Gulf Coast season. Pick regularly at 4-8 inches for the best texture in gumbo, frying, and pickling.
sources: Vegetable Cultivar Descriptions for North America (NC State University)

planting.note: Direct sow after soil is reliably warm; tall plants need a long, hot season to produce their characteristic long pods.

directions: Cherokee Long Pod is a Southern heirloom preserved through an Oklahoma seed-saving family and maintained by heirloom seed banks as a regional keeper variety. Plants grow to around 6 feet and produce light-green pods that can reach 15 inches in length while the plant continues to flower and set new pods over a long season. For the most tender eating, harvest well before pods reach their maximum length, around 4-6 inches, and pick frequently to keep plants productive through the heat of summer.

planting.note: Direct sow once soil has warmed; this Gulf South-bred selection is well adapted to Louisiana's heat and humidity.

directions: Louisiana Market okra was developed at a Louisiana agricultural research station and entered All-America Selections trials in 1950, bred for Gulf South market growers wanting heavy, reliable yields. The plants carry their pods where foliage and flower stalks part readily, making harvest faster and more efficient for market picking. Pods are thick-walled, smooth, and green, best picked at 3-4 inches for tenderness; the variety performs well in the long, humid growing season typical of southern Louisiana.
sources: Vegetable Cultivar Descriptions for North America (NC State University)

planting.note: Direct sow in warm soil; semi-dwarf habit suits closer spacing than tall cowhorn-type okras.

directions: Campbell's Long Green is a mid-20th-century processing okra bred for uniform, slender, deep-green pods with strong color retention, and it later served as breeding stock for other canning-type okra selections. The semi-dwarf plants are compact relative to older heirloom cowhorn types, making them easier to manage in a home garden row. Pick pods at 3-5 inches for best tenderness and continue harvesting every couple of days to keep plants setting new pods through the heat of summer.
sources: Vegetable Cultivar Descriptions for North America (NC State University)

planting.note: Direct sow in warm soil; valued where whitefly-transmitted yellow vein mosaic virus is a regional problem for okra.

directions: Parbhani Kranti is a widely grown Indian okra release bred from a backcross of the wild relative Abelmoschus manihot into the cultivar Pusa Sawani, giving it strong resistance to yellow vein mosaic virus, a serious whitefly-transmitted disease that can devastate susceptible okra crops. Plants are tall and single-stemmed with dark-green foliage, flowering around 45-50 days and ready for first harvest near 55 days. Pods are slender and dark green, best picked young for the most tender texture; this variety outyielded older standard cultivars in multi-site Indian field trials.
sources: peer-reviewed okra yellow vein mosaic virus resistance trials
